races.name: Zyn In-The-Moment Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Zyn Pacesetter British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Superior Choice
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good and showed prominently in all runs; the Gosden yard is in solid 14-day form (9/34) and this horse is shortest in trip terms from his last win — he has the class to control from the front but his OR=120 will be tested if rivals quicken late.|

runners_data.name: Act Of Generosity
runners_data.note: Roger Varian runner who finished fifth on his only start over 10f on Good, so the step to 1m2f is logical but he remains lightly exposed; a natural hold-up type, he will need more pace than Superior Choice is likely to generate to produce his best run.|

runners_data.name: Hatteen
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's charge holds genuine hold-up form (two seconds at 10f on Good) but is redistributed to midfield on the pace map because the field's rear is already congested with hold-up types — his natural style is from the back, and he may find himself racing closer than ideal without the cover he needs.|

runners_data.name: Ragazzo Grandi
runners_data.note: A complete unknown on running style with no accessible race history and a trainer (Hilal Kobeissi) showing just 0/1 in the 14-day window; the going is marked UNKNOWN for this horse and any tactical surprise he brings — positive or negative — is impossible to price with confidence.|

runners_data.name: Zurna
runners_data.note: Julia & Shelley Birkett's filly has run seventh and ninth on soft ground over 10f, so the upgrade to Good at 1m2f is a clear positive on paper; however, the form base is modest and her hold-up profile means she requires more pace than this race is likely to offer.|

races.paceDynamic: Superior Choice is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this five-runner field and, with no rival likely to press him hard from the outset, he should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m2f Good-ground trip at Newmarket's July course. Act Of Generosity, Hatteen, and Zurna are all hold-up types by profile, meaning the race defaults to a single-paced leader who can set his own rhythm without being harassed through the early and middle sections. Ragazzo Grandi is an unknown quantity on style, but with no other front-runner to challenge Superior Choice for the lead, the pace is unlikely to be genuinely hot — a moderate-to-fair tempo is the most probable outcome. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel close to the pace and produce a sustained finish over those who rely on a truly fast, pressured gallop to bring their late kick into play, giving the advantage to any runner able to sit just off the leader rather than hunt from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Superior Choice secures the lead unchallenged and sets a fair but unhurried pace throughout.
scenarios.body: If Superior Choice secures the lead unchallenged and sets a fair but unhurried pace throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Ragazzo Grandi or a prominent-travelling runner makes smooth headway to challenge Superior Choice before the turn.
scenarios.body: If Ragazzo Grandi or a prominent-travelling runner makes smooth headway to challenge Superior Choice before the turn.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string out the field and leave ground for hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string out the field and leave ground for hold-up horses to close.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Or Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Ragazzo Grandi or another runner disrupts the early order, causing a false start or a break in rhythm that scrambles positions.
scenarios.body: If Ragazzo Grandi or another runner disrupts the early order, causing a false start or a break in rhythm that scrambles positions.

watchPoints.text: Superior Choice — watch whether he is allowed to bowl along uncontested; if he faces no early pressure from Ragazzo Grandi, his controlled tempo could simply be too slow to bring the hold-up horses into the race at all.

Ragazzo Grandi — unknown style and an inexperienced trainer combination means his early behaviour and positioning could materially alter the race shape; any prominent move by him changes the pace calculus significantly.

Act Of Generosity and Zurna — both hold-up types who need a genuine gallop that this race is unlikely to produce; if either drifts wide looking for cover or runs too freely, their chances are further compromised.

Hatteen — his redistribution to midfield on the map is worth noting in-running; if he is forced to race closer than his natural style, watch whether Rob Hornby drops him back deliberately early or gets caught in an awkward middle position with no momentum.

races.name: Zyn Pole Position Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Madame De Sevigne
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare whose recent form reads poorly (7-8-3-7-10) and whose best sim-going returns are modest; the Newmarket straight track at 7f could expose her tendency to come from deep in fields where the pace suits closers, and there is no obvious reason from trainer or jockey angle to upgrade her chance here.

runners_data.name: Bravo Zulu
runners_data.note: Placed twice recently on Good ground at 6f for Loughnane, and while a natural hold-up type, she has the tactical flexibility and recent form to suggest she could slot into a workable position if the field spreads; the step back to 7f from 6f should suit, and this is arguably her best opportunity of the card.

runners_data.name: Stenmark
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with consistent placed form over 7f on Good and Standard, sitting comfortably in his natural slot just off the pace; Carson rides a tidy race tactically and the horse's profile is a good fit for a well-strung-out race shape behind one leader.

runners_data.name: Potomac River
runners_data.note: Ran well to finish second over this course and distance on Good ground on only his second turf start, which is encouraging, but he is a natural hold-up type being compressed into a field with several similar rivals; the 37-day absence adds a small query and his best chance relies on more end-to-end pace than Gallant alone is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Cherry Cobbler
runners_data.note: Won over this exact course and distance on Good ground, which is the standout course-and-distance qualifier in the field; Tudhope is an astute jockey who may find a way to deploy her more prominently than her hold-up label suggests, and that piece of C&D form on matching going keeps her highly relevant despite the redistribution squeeze at the rear.

runners_data.name: Dashing Dick
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has finished in the top two only once in 15 recent starts on Good ground, with most of his wins coming on Soft; his preferred 6f trip and weak Good-ground record make 7f at Newmarket a tough ask, and he sits deep in the field as a genuine hold-up type in a crowded rear group.

runners_data.name: Eazy On The Eye
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4yo who has placed twice over 8f on Standard for Heather Main, a trainer whose 0/9 last-14-day record is noted; the 54-day absence is the longest in the field, and while the drop to 7f on Good ground might suit, the freshness and unknown readiness are meaningful concerns.

runners_data.name: Gallant
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter, operating slightly out of his comfort zone at 7f after a career mostly over 5-6f for Oli Rix; he carries top weight at 137lbs and recent form (6-2-6-11-7) includes only one placing, but his tactical role as the unchallenged leader makes him structurally significant regardless of raw ability — the STYLE_FIT tag is a reminder his finishing kick under pressure is unproven at this trip.

runners_data.name: Miletus
runners_data.note: Well-weighted prominent racer with multiple places over 7f on varying going, including a second here on Good for James Keane; the 8-day turnaround is short but the horse ran only 8 days ago and clearly trains quickly, and his position just behind the pace is his natural slot — a clean run from that position makes him a key figure.

runners_data.name: Dapper Guest
runners_data.note: Has won over 7f on Good ground but his recent form (4-9-0-8-6) is poor, and his 10/15 Good-ground record in simulation is the worst in the field; the visor (headgear flag v) is noted and Egan is capable of a positive ride, but the form needs to be taken on trust after a sequence of disappointing efforts.

races.paceDynamic: Gallant is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, he should stride into a comfortable, uncontested position from the outset on Newmarket's July Course straight seven furlongs. The pace he sets will be honest but controlled — a lone leader on Good ground rarely crawls, yet with no pressure he can dictate every yard to the Dip and beyond. Prominently-placed Stenmark and Miletus are the most likely to track Gallant in second and third, giving the race a well-strung-out shape rather than a bunched cavalry charge. This race shape most favours prominent racers who can sit just off the controlled pace and produce a clean, sustained run from two furlongs out — pure closers will need to find a lot of ground on a track that does not traditionally reward horses making up significant distances from the rear in handicaps. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the back: Potomac River, Cherry Cobbler, Dashing Dick, Eazy On The Eye, Dapper Guest and Bravo Zulu are all genuine hold-up horses competing for the same rear positions, with Cherry Cobbler (who has won over this course and distance on Good) and Bravo Zulu (recent 6f Good form) the most likely to find a workable position if any of the group can benefit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gallant Leads, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Gallant sets a fair but unhurried pace and the winner comes from the group that tracks him in the first three or four.
scenarios.body: If Gallant sets a fair but unhurried pace and the winner comes from the group that tracks him in the first three or four.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely generous enough to stretch the field and create a true end-to-end gallop that a late-finisher can exploit.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely generous enough to stretch the field and create a true end-to-end gallop that a late-finisher can exploit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Gallant Sustains Gallop Home
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely modest throughout and Gallant, left fully unchallenged, simply bowls along and is never reeled in.
scenarios.body: If the tempo is genuinely modest throughout and Gallant, left fully unchallenged, simply bowls along and is never reeled in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Gallant sets a false pace or stops dramatically, causing the field to concertina in the final two furlongs with an unexpected result.
scenarios.body: If Gallant sets a false pace or stops dramatically, causing the field to concertina in the final two furlongs with an unexpected result.

watchPoints.text: Cherry Cobbler is the form horse at this course and distance on matching going — watch Tudhope for any attempt to push forward early rather than settling in the rear pack, as a prominent position would dramatically improve her winning chance.

Gallant carries 137lbs as top weight on a straight track where he is stretching his stamina envelope over 7f; if he fades sharply inside the final furlong, the horses tracking him most closely (Stenmark, Miletus) will be the immediate beneficiaries.

The cluster of hold-up types — Potomac River, Dashing Dick, Eazy On The Eye, Dapper Guest, Bravo Zulu and Madame De Sevigne — will all be jostling for the same rear ground; watch for traffic problems at the two-furlong pole where this straight track can become congested as the field fans.

Miletus runs for the second time in 8 days — watch for any market drift that might signal the quick turnaround is a concern, or conversely any support that confirms trainer Keane is happy with the horse after last week's run.

Eazy On The Eye returns after 54 days for Heather Main, whose 14-day trainer record of 0/9 is the weakest in the field; watch whether Harry Vigors (7lb claimer) attempts to compensate for freshness by taking a prominent position early, which would be against the horse's hold-up profile.

races.name: Zyn Pole Position Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Physique
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer for Micky Fenton who needs horses to come back to her; recent form string of 7-0032 suggests she is struggling to land a blow at present and her best sim-going figures here (0W3P) show place ability but no win punch at this level.

runners_data.name: Benacre
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's six-year-old wants a prominent position and handles good ground well, but his form string 603550 is unimpressive and a 3-5 record on similar going with no wins is a concern; Jack Callan's 3lb claim is some compensation.

runners_data.name: Fifty Nifty
runners_data.note: Chelsea Banham's five-year-old wears a hood and has two wins on similar going from ten runs, suggesting conditions suit even if the recent 0654-7 form is uninspiring; Joey Haynes takes the ride and the horse's hold-up style means it needs things to fall right late.

runners_data.name: Drifts Away
runners_data.note: Returning from a 295-day absence for T J Kent, which is a significant fitness question mark; showed a win and a second in the form string before the break and has place form on good ground, but prominent-running horses resuming after nearly ten months are often short of race sharpness.

runners_data.name: Great Mates
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners this four-year-old who has a genuine win at 8f on good and is naturally a front-running/prominent type — the depth of prominent runners in this field means he is unlikely to secure his preferred position and will be racing against his instincts, which must temper his chance.

runners_data.name: Noble Guest
runners_data.note: George Margarson's four-year-old is authentically a hold-up horse by style and has shown one win and three places from nine runs on good or similar; placed to run from midfield against its natural grain today, so the tactical setup is working against it despite decent going credentials.

runners_data.name: Al Karrar
runners_data.note: The highest-rated runner in the field at OR 82, returning 30 days after a run, and the one horse confirmed to set the pace; his last five runs have come over 6f on mainly soft or standard ground, so stepping to 7f on good at Newmarket is a slight query, but Tom Clover has him spot-on at the weights.

runners_data.name: Best Rate
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's four-year-old is lightly freshed up after just eight days and has a consistent prominent style at 7f; his T14 strike rate of 10/42 is the strongest in the field and he arrives in the best recent winning form of the prominent group, though he has not broken his duck at this distance on any going.

runners_data.name: Longlai
runners_data.note: George Baker's seven-year-old has been off 226 days and that extended absence is a major concern; hold-up style by profile and recent form 30070- is weak, while his best sim-going placing of 3/8f/GOO came at a longer trip — this looks like a reappearance run rather than a winning one.

races.paceDynamic: Al Karrar is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to press him from the outset, Dougie Costello can dictate a controlled, honest gallop over this 7f Newmarket July course on good ground — a tempo that is sustainable rather than scorching. Best Rate and Benacre are the likeliest to slot in just off Al Karrar's heels, with Drifts Away also likely to want a prominent berth after a long absence. The field contains more genuinely prominent types than the map can accommodate: Great Mates is a natural front-runner who will be squeezed to midfield against his instincts, and Noble Guest — a true hold-up horse — is also mapped out of natural role, meaning neither is likely to be racing where it wants to be. A controlled front-running pace on a fair surface at Newmarket favours horses who can travel prominently and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, giving the advantage to confirmed prominent racers and those proven over the trip on good ground rather than closers relying on a collapse from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Al Karrar Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Al Karrar is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a measured gallop and the field cannot close the gap in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Al Karrar is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a measured gallop and the field cannot close the gap in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challengers Overhaul Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fractionally stronger than Al Karrar intends, allowing Best Rate or Benacre to edge past inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace is just fractionally stronger than Al Karrar intends, allowing Best Rate or Benacre to edge past inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves genuinely strong enough to set up a late run from the back markers.
scenarios.body: If the early pace proves genuinely strong enough to set up a late run from the back markers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Outsider Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the race unfolds untidily with several prominent types interfering with each other's position and a rank outsider takes advantage of the gaps.
scenarios.body: If the race unfolds untidily with several prominent types interfering with each other's position and a rank outsider takes advantage of the gaps.

watchPoints.text: Al Karrar (Dougie Costello) — watch whether he gets a completely unchallenged lead from the off; if Benacre or Best Rate push forward to press him, the pace lifts and the race shape changes dramatically.

Great Mates — a natural front-runner drawn into a field too full of prominent types; watch for early crowding or interference as multiple horses attempt to claim the same ground in the first furlong, which could disrupt several runners simultaneously.

Drifts Away — returning from 295 days off, watch the market move before the off; any significant support would suggest the stable believes fitness is not an issue, but blind faith in a 10-month absentee over 7f on good is risky.

Best Rate (Richard Hannon, T14: 10/42) — the strongest in-form trainer in the race by recent strike rate; watch for any market support as Hannon's yard is firing and this horse arrives the freshest of the prominent group at just 8 days between runs.

Longlai — 226 days absent and modest recent form; if it shows unusually well in the market it may be a stable confidence indicator, but as it stands this looks a race where it re-finds its legs rather than wins.

races.name: Zyn Frontrunner Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Hard To Believe
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 3yo has won over 10f at Staymix and 8f on soft, making this 1m4f step up a potential question mark on stamina, though the good ground suits; Rob Hornby rides and the horse is likely to push forward and press Outback Legend, making him a key player if the trip is within range.

runners_data.name: Outback Legend
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on soft last time for the Newland & Insole yard and that stamina form translates well to this trip on good ground; Zac Lloyd can dictate his own terms as the sole confirmed front-runner, and while his style fit score reflects the pace map complexity, he is the one horse guaranteed to get his natural position at the head of affairs.

runners_data.name: Brave Hunter
runners_data.note: Ismail Mohammed's 3yo has placed twice over 8f on good ground, his best form coming at shorter trips, and while he is a naturally prominent horse, the presence of Outback Legend and Hard To Believe makes it hard for him to secure that early position; his racing style is genuinely front-running in nature, but the race shape pushes him back, which is not where his form profile suggests he performs best.

runners_data.name: Temple
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's 3yo drops back from a 12f run at Sandown and holds a placed effort at 8f on soft; Sorin Moldoveanu takes the 7lb claim and the horse's hold-up style means he needs the pace to be genuine to make ground, which is not guaranteed with Outback Legend likely to control tempo — 55 days between runs is also worth noting.

runners_data.name: Outflank
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's 3yo has placed in three consecutive starts over 10-12f including on good ground at Newmarket, so course, distance and going all stack up positively; Luke Catton's 3lb claim is an asset, the hood goes on, and the unknown style tag suggests tactical flexibility — consistent placed form makes this one a player if the pace develops honestly.

runners_data.name: Battosai
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's 3yo has placed over 10f twice on good ground and arrives freshest in the field at 14 days since last run, but the blinkered type is at heart a front-running horse whose prominent inclinations are accommodated by the redistribution here; at OR 72 he is the lowest-rated runner and would need things to go very right from an awkward mapped position to feature.

races.paceDynamic: Outback Legend is the confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a six-runner field over 1m4f on good ground at Newmarket, the expectation is a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset rather than a searching test. Hard To Believe will look to sit prominently behind Outback Legend, creating a small cluster at the head of affairs while Temple, Outflank, and the redistributed pair hold their ground further back. The field contains more prominent types than can physically occupy those early positions — Brave Hunter and Battosai are genuine up-with-the-pace horses in profile but are mapped to midfield given the race shape, meaning they are unlikely to influence tempo or secure their natural position. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a measured gallop over a staying trip — strongly favours horses with proven stamina who can travel smoothly just off the pace and produce a sustained late effort, rather than pure hold-up closers who would need a truly honest pace to set up their finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Outback Legend Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Outback Legend gets a clean break and settles into an uncontested rhythm, dictating a measured pace that suits his stamina profile.
scenarios.body: If Outback Legend gets a clean break and settles into an uncontested rhythm, dictating a measured pace that suits his stamina profile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Hard To Believe pushes forward early and applies pressure to Outback Legend, turning it into a two-horse battle from the front.
scenarios.body: If Hard To Believe pushes forward early and applies pressure to Outback Legend, turning it into a two-horse battle from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front pair go too fast for the distance and the pace collapses in the straight, allowing hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: If the front pair go too fast for the distance and the pace collapses in the straight, allowing hold-up horses to close.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Disrupt Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Brave Hunter or Battosai push forward unexpectedly early and inject pace they cannot sustain over 1m4f, scrambling the race shape.
scenarios.body: If Brave Hunter or Battosai push forward unexpectedly early and inject pace they cannot sustain over 1m4f, scrambling the race shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Hard To Believe pushes forward to challenge Outback Legend early — if Hornby elects to press the front-runner from the outset, the race shape changes materially and the moderate pace assumption breaks down.

Brave Hunter and Battosai are both genuine prominent types crammed into midfield by the race shape; if either forces their way forward at the start, it injects unexpected tempo over a trip neither has convincingly stayed.

Temple's 55-day absence for Jane Chapple-Hyam warrants monitoring in the paddock — fitness queries on a hold-up horse in a race likely to be run at a restrained pace compound the tactical disadvantage.

Outflank's consistent placed record over 10-12f on similar ground with the hood added makes him a horse to track through the first half of the race — if he travels smoothly in the pack, he is well positioned if the pace picks up in the straight.

races.name: Zyn Frontrunner Finish Handicap

runners_data.name: Spell Master
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has placed twice from four runs on Good going at 7f, and trainer Oli Rix fires at 25% over 14 days; stepping to a mile for the first time is the key query, as all five career runs have been at 7f, and he is naturally drawn into the prominent slots directly behind the leader here.

runners_data.name: Exposure
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's yard is among the classiest operations in the field (T14: 10/29) and this 4yo has solid AW form at 8f; she is genuinely a prominent racer by nature but will find herself shuffled into midfield by the sheer volume of pace ahead — her 249-day absence after a string of AW runs makes it hard to know where she returns.

runners_data.name: Stem
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner whose best finishes have been two runner-up efforts on Soft ground at 8f; naturally wants to race close to the pace but is pushed back by a crowded prominent section — the switch from Soft to Good could also limit his effectiveness, with no win or placed effort on a similar surface in five career runs.

runners_data.name: Mythical Guest
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who has placed four times in fifteen runs on similar going but never won on Good; Olivia Haines claims 7lbs which matters in a competitive handicap, though his Soft-going form is superior and he will be waiting for late openings that may not materialise if the pace is controlled.

runners_data.name: Arctic Thunder
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 5yo naturally races prominently but is squeezed into midfield by the numbers here; recent form shows two straight 6th-7th finishes on Good and Soft, and while he has one win on similar going he is hard to back at his current trajectory, racing out of his preferred position in a field this competitive.

runners_data.name: Fort Rock
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's 3yo is the highest-profile youngster in the race, unbeaten in two starts on Tapeta at Wolverhampton before placing at Goodwood on Good; headgear worn previously (p), and racing off just 49 days, he will press forward from the front rank — if his quality translates to handicap company on turf, he makes the race.

runners_data.name: Synners Kid
runners_data.note: Lemos De Souza's 3yo won twice consecutively on Soft/AW at 8f but has since posted back-to-back 6th-place finishes on Good; he will try to press forward, but a going preference for softer conditions and no placed effort on Good ground in five runs makes this surface a live question.

runners_data.name: Elan d'Or
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' 3yo is a natural front-runner — two wins came wire-to-wire on AW at Wolverhampton — but the prominent section is full and he is mapped behind it; if he can push forward and make his position, he becomes dangerous, but racing off his natural style is a material discount.

runners_data.name: Loz Vegas
runners_data.note: Hold-up 3yo from Peter Chapple-Hyam's yard who won at a mile on Good at Brighton; George Wood rides and the stable has a thin 14-day record (0/2), but she has shown she stays the trip and acts on the surface — her main task is whether she can sustain a run through a compressed mid-race group.

runners_data.name: Magnatura
runners_data.note: Tom Ward's 3yo has two wins (7f and 1m) on Good and AW and has placed at 8f on Good — solid profile, but a genuine prominent racer who will find herself in midfield given the crowded pace section; her best form has come when bowling along, and racing off the pace in a field with a single controlled front-runner slightly dulls her chance.

runners_data.name: Ramli
runners_data.note: Listed as a NON-RUNNER — disregard entirely for race shape analysis; if declared, he is a prominent type with only a handful of runs and limited pattern of evidence.

runners_data.name: Sterling Knight
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's 7yo is the most experienced hold-up horse in the race and won at this exact track and distance (8f, Good, Newmarket July) in his last victory; Jack Callan's 3lb claim helps in a handicap, and though recent form shows inconsistency his course-and-distance profile is the most directly relevant of any closer here.

runners_data.name: Spanish Voice
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 4yo is confirmed as the lone front-runner and will lead from the outset on Good turf at Newmarket's July mile; won twice including at 8f and 10f on similar ground, has a STYLE_FIT tag suggesting he may face pressure if rivals push him, but with no genuine rival for the lead that pressure looks unlikely to materialise — he gets to set the tempo on his own terms.

runners_data.name: Angel Hunter
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's 4yo wears a hood (b) and has one win at 8f on AW; placed twice but five runs on Good have produced a mixed bag (5th, 6th, 6th, 7th, 8th), and the headgear and 20-day freshener give him a yard angle worth noting even if his recent Good-ground profile is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Release The Storm
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's 4yo has won both career turf starts on Good ground at 7f and has a clean 2W record on this surface; Harry Vigors claims 7lbs and the 41-day absence is the only mild concern — a horse who has done nothing but win or fail to complete on Good turf, stepping up to a mile, whose profile screams suitability for a steadily-run front-rank race.

runners_data.name: Dark Tornado
runners_data.note: Michael Wigham's 5yo wears a visor (v) and has an outstanding 11-from-11 record on Good going with two wins; J F Egan takes the ride and this horse has been placed five times from eleven Good-ground starts — the consistent form on this surface and distance profile make him the most reliable hold-up candidate if the closers ever get their run.

races.paceDynamic: Spanish Voice is the lone confirmed front-runner and will stride straight to the front from the off, setting a measured, uncontested gallop on Good turf over a mile on the Bunbury Mile course at Newmarket's July track — a configuration that rarely sees truly strong early fractions without a genuine pace duel. With no rival able to contest the lead freely, Spanish Voice will control the tempo and can dictate precisely how hard this race is run, meaning the pace is likely to be sustainable rather than pressurising. Fort Rock, Spell Master, Angel Hunter, Release The Storm, and Synners Kid will push into the prominent slots directly behind, while the hold-up contingent of Sterling Knight, Dark Tornado, Mythical Guest, and Loz Vegas will settle in rear, facing a real task if the leader never fully extends the field. This field contains significantly more pace than the map can accommodate — Elan d'Or, Exposure, Stem, Arctic Thunder, Magnatura, and Ramli are all genuine prominent racers but have been redistributed to midfield positions because they cannot all secure their natural spot; of these, Elan d'Or and Exposure, with the highest profile form, are most likely to actually push forward if gaps open early. The race shape strongly favours horses that can travel close to a controlled pace and produce a clean turn-of-foot in the final two furlongs — prominent racers who land in the slipstream of Spanish Voice without burning energy are best placed.

watchPoints.text: Spanish Voice leads unopposed — watch whether Callum Hutchinson elects to inject a mid-race injection of pace or dawdles; if he dawdles, the finish will be a sprint and his rivals' turn-of-foot becomes decisive rather than his stamina advantage.

Elan d'Or and Exposure are natural prominent horses mapped to midfield — watch the first two furlongs to see whether either pushes forward aggressively, because if they do they could disrupt the expected settled prominent order and alter tempo calculations entirely.

Release The Storm is 41 days off and steps up from 7f to a mile for the first time — watch whether Harry Vigors (7lb claimer) can get him to settle early in a large field, as his two wins have come front-running at a shorter trip and he must show he stays.

Sterling Knight's record shows a win at this exact track and distance on Good ground — watch where Jack Callan positions him in the early stages; if he is shuffled further back than usual in a 16-runner field, his closing run from the Dip becomes significantly harder to execute.

Fort Rock is Charlie Appleby's sole runner and has raced exclusively on artificial surfaces before his Goodwood placing — watch his paddock demeanour and early jumping behaviour, as first-time exposure to a true turf handicap field of 16 can catch inexperienced horses off guard regardless of raw ability.

races.name: Zyn Strong Stride Handicap

runners_data.name: Phantom Watch
runners_data.note: Hood (hg:v) fitted for concentration; hold-up specialist who has placed at 8f on Soft/Standard and arrives after a 140-day break, so fitness is the key question — Daniel Tudhope adds experience but Tudhope/Palmer's 14-day strike rate of 1 from 9 is modest.|

runners_data.name: Crimson Rambler
runners_data.note: Ran well to finish second and third in recent Good-ground miles, showing he handles this surface; his natural style is a rear-tracking hold-up horse, and with so many closers in the field he is unlikely to get the clean, unimpeded run that brings out his best — discount him unless the pace genuinely tests the leader.|

runners_data.name: Mimi's Magic
runners_data.note: Unknown style classification (U) leaves her tactically flexible; Ed Dunlop's yard is running at 2/13 over 14 days, and her single run on Good ground produced a win, making that form angle interesting — at 1m she steps up from her recent 8f efforts and could find the trip stretching.|

runners_data.name: Jamie Sommers
runners_data.note: Consistent form string with multiple placed efforts at 8f on Good, but her strongest finishes have come when getting a clear passage — in this field, her natural hold-up inclination will be squeezed by rival closers occupying similar ground, and the redistribution to midfield reflects a realistic positional compromise.|

runners_data.name: Hurricane Laughter
runners_data.note: Lightly raced two-year-old (now three) returning from a 205-day absence with only three runs on the book, all at 7f on Standard or Good; stepping up to a mile on this comeback makes her an unknown quantity, and the lack of an established style (U) means she offers limited pace-map value.|

runners_data.name: Malika
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's yard is in good form at 7/52, and Rob Hornby is a strong booking; but Malika has only three handicap runs, all showing mid-to-rear finishes, and her hold-up tendency means she shares the same congested closing ground as several rivals — only a perfectly timed move through the field will bring her into contention.|

runners_data.name: Guest House
runners_data.note: The most interesting hold-up horse in the field on the evidence: one win and two places from six outings all on Good ground, with a course-form win (1/8f/GOO) boosting her claims at this track; despite being mapped to midfield due to redistribution, she is a genuine closer whose Good-ground record is the best of the rear-runners.|

runners_data.name: Crafty Blue
runners_data.note: Dropped from OR=70 despite a 7f win on Standard; his last two handicap runs at 8f on Standard/Soft produced finishing positions of 9 and 9, suggesting he needs a quicker surface and may not truly stay a mile — Alec Voikhansky is a claim jockey which adds further risk.|

runners_data.name: Royal Bodyguard
runners_data.note: Three placed finishes in recent form including a second and a third at 8f and 10f, and his Good-going record shows two places from four runs; Michael Bell's 2/23 14-day figure is modest, but Royal Bodyguard's positional versatility and willingness to race prominently makes him one of the few who can genuinely press Safe Harbor.|

runners_data.name: Safe Harbor
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, holding a STYLE_FIT note suggesting he may be nudged out of role under pressure, but with no rival to challenge for the lead that concern is largely academic — two consecutive runner-up finishes on Good ground at 8f underpin his form, and Jack Gilligan has a clean route to dictate from the front.|

races.paceDynamic: Safe Harbor is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should stride into an uncontested position from the outset, setting a sustainable gallop on Good ground over Newmarket's July course mile. The field is dominated by hold-up types — Crimson Rambler, Jamie Sommers, Malika, and Guest House are all natural hold-up horses who have been pushed into a midfield mapping simply because there are too many closers for the map to accommodate at the rear; in reality, they will be jostling for ground behind a lone pace-setter rather than tracking comfortably. This creates a race where the early sectionals are likely to be honest but not frantic, with Safe Harbor controlling tempo from the front and a cluttered midfield-to-rear group unable to all find their natural rhythm. The race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or within striking range of Safe Harbor, as the steady pace rewards runners who can latch onto the leader without burning petrol — deep hold-up horses will face a stern test of getting competitive in time.

scenarios.body: If Safe Harbor bowls along uncontested and the pace is honest without becoming a sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Safe Harbor sets every fraction alone — watch whether Jack Gilligan elects to dawdle and set up a sprint or commit to a true pace, as that single decision determines which scenario unfolds.

Guest House has the best Good-ground course record among the hold-up horses; if she finds a clear passage through the compressed midfield in the final two furlongs she could outfinish the pack, so watch her position rounding the final marker.

Royal Bodyguard is the most plausible horse to track Safe Harbor at a safe distance; if he moves up to second spot by halfway he becomes dangerous, so watch whether Ross Coakley positions him forward from the outset.

Crimson Rambler and Jamie Sommers are both natural hold-up types who will be bunched together in a crowded middle group — traffic and interference between them is a real risk that could nullify either horse's finishing effort regardless of ability.

Hurricane Laughter returns from 205 days off and steps up in trip for the first time; watch how she travels in the early stages, as a free-going move early on a quick reappearance could leave her empty in the closing stages.

races.name: Find Your Zyn Moment Handicap

runners_data.name: Fiscal Policy
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has won over this C&D in Good conditions; Ruth Carr yard out of form (T14: 0/32) but this horse is perfectly placed tactically as the lone pace-setter; STYLE_FIT tag suggests she's being asked to fill the lead role entirely, which suits but also means she carries all the pace responsibility.

runners_data.name: Ancient State
runners_data.note: Sharp 5f winner on Standard who steps up to 6f on Good turf; Adam Kirby trained (T14: 1/14) with no recent Good-ground form to speak of (0W0P in similar going); headgear noted; may find this trip and surface a stretch from recent Tapeta form.

runners_data.name: Spring Bloom
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer with excellent Good-ground record (11/15 runners placed); hold-up style suits a true closer scenario; at age 9 she needs things to set up perfectly, and in this large field her Callum Hutchinson partnership needs a clear lane in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Rebel Path
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up horse with limited recent form (773 last three); Stuart Williams yard struggling (T14: 0/22) and 34-day break adds query; sim-going record moderate; Olivia Haines claims 7lb which helps the weight, but recent efforts offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: State Of Madness
runners_data.note: Prominent-style horse who acts on Good ground and has hit the frame recently; Mark Loughnane yard showing (T14: 1/15) and 34-day gap to manage; races close to pace and will be competing for a prominent pitch from stall, making him a genuine each-way threat if getting his natural position.

runners_data.name: Jimmy Knocker
runners_data.note: Won on Soft but has placed on Good, though his true form is for the softer end; hold-up style with headgear (t flag); Kyle McHugh claims 7lb; 25-day absence is manageable, but Good ground is less favourable than his winning conditions.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Jenny
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with four places from five Good/similar-ground runs and a recent win on Standard; Steph Hollinshead yard flat (T14: 0/12) but the horse's own profile is strong for this race shape — consistently places when racing just off a pace-setter at 6f.

runners_data.name: Ancient Times
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse off 197 days and showing moderate recent form (0-0-6-12-10 last five); headgear (t) applied; long absence from George Wood is a significant concern, and Good ground does suit but the layoff length makes confidence difficult regardless.

runners_data.name: Zoulu Warrior
runners_data.note: Won twice on Standard going; hold-up style and 119-day break is a real question mark; headgear (p); Harry Vigors claims 7lb; turf Good form limited and the extended absence combined with a move to turf makes this a speculative entry with positional concerns in a large field.

runners_data.name: Northcliff
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 7f on Good ground and carries a strong winning record (4W5P sim-going); genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield position on the map as the field is over-stocked with closers — his natural race position is further back, so discount his chance in this shape accordingly; Rob Hornby takes the ride.

runners_data.name: Havana Sky
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop yard showing recent improvement (T14: 2/17); placed at 7f on Tapeta but all recent Newmarket form on Standard; a true hold-up horse whose racing position in this field will be compromised by the volume of closers — unlikely to get her preferred deep, patient pitch.

runners_data.name: Way To Dubai
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby yard with one recent winner (T14: 1/23) and Benoit De La Sayette riding; all sim-going runs without a win or place (0W0P), which is telling; this horse's hold-up style will be squeezed in a field already over-populated with rear-of-field types, and 52 days off adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: Currahee
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced two-year-old (the youngest runner in the field) off 283 days; won twice and placed twice over 6-7f on Good and Standard; hold-up natural who will not get his preferred position in this race — the long absence from Simon Pearce's small yard is the biggest risk factor.

runners_data.name: Clasina
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer over 7f who is dropping to 6f here; John Berry yard quiet (T14: 0/5); 299-day absence is the most significant concern in the race; her Good-ground record is solid (10/15 runners in similar going placed) but the layoff and trip drop make expectations modest.

runners_data.name: Elvetham
runners_data.note: Prominent-style horse with headgear (b) and excellent recent consistency (placed in 5 of last 6); Conrad Allen yard flat (T14: 0/7); acts on Good turf and has placed at this trip; only 9 days since last run but that shows freshness; genuine tactical contender for a prominent position.

runners_data.name: Mart
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose redistributed map position reflects a field too full of closers to get a true rear draw; Dylan Cunha yard showing (T14: 2/25); only one sim-going run (0W0P) and a modest 6f profile overall; Zac Lloyd rides, and the 9-day turnaround suggests connections are keen.

runners_data.name: Grand Citadel
runners_data.note: Prominent style with headgear (b) and progressive recent form (945321 last six, including a win); Micky Fenton yard (T14: 0/3); dropped in grade and has clearly been freshened; Grace McEntee rides and this horse's willingness to race positively gives it live claims in the prominent group.

runners_data.name: Rainbow Sorbet
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse off 21 days with only four runs to her name; Jim & Suzi Best yard in form (T14: 2/5); Olivia Tubb claims 5lb; sim-going record thin (2/4) and the redistribution away from her natural position will make it hard to produce her best — the trainer form angle is the one positive to note.

races.paceDynamic: Fiscal Policy is the one confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner field and, with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge, should stride into a controlled lead from the break and set a honest but manageable tempo on Good ground at Newmarket's July course. State Of Madness, Spirit Of Jenny, Ancient State, and Elvetham are all prominent-style horses who will press for position behind Fiscal Policy, creating a competitive early contest for the front ranks without necessarily generating a truly brutal gallop. The field is heavily weighted towards hold-up types, but the redistribution of Northcliff, Havana Sky, Way To Dubai, Currahee, Clasina, Mart, and Rainbow Sorbet — all genuine closers who are unlikely to secure their natural rear-of-field position in this large, pace-sparse field — means true closers will be bunched in the middle and early movers from the prominent group will have a decisive advantage. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or just off the pace, as the uncontested early leader Fiscal Policy sets a sustainable tempo that will be hard to reel in from a true hold-up position over six furlongs on flat Newmarket ground.

scenarios.body: If an unexpected pace collapse or early traffic trouble leaves a true hold-up horse a clear, unobstructed run to sprint home late.

watchPoints.text: Fiscal Policy holds a clean, uncontested lead from the break — watch whether she is able to stride clear into a rhythm unchallenged, as if she does the race may already be won by the time the field turns for home.

The sheer volume of hold-up horses (Northcliff, Havana Sky, Way To Dubai, Currahee, Clasina, Mart, Rainbow Sorbet) redistributed into midfield creates serious congestion — watch for traffic trouble from three furlongs out as jockeys simultaneously seek racing room.

Grand Citadel's headgear and recent progressive form (three consecutive places into a win) makes this horse a dark threat if the prominent group burns itself out — watch whether Grace McEntee tracks the leader closely from the outset.

Spirit Of Jenny has placed four times from five Good/similar-going starts — watch her position in the early stages as Dougie Costello will look to sit second or third on the fence behind Fiscal Policy, the exact position this race shape rewards.

Ancient Times returns from 197 days off with headgear applied and is the longest-absent runner in the race — watch the market moves for this Harry Eustace representative, as significant support would indicate stable confidence despite the absence.
